summary: Name the date and number forms exempt from sanitisation instead of deducing them from the characters, and send an ISBN in both spellings the archive stores.
reason: The first version of the guard exempted any value made only of digits and separators, and an ISBN-13 written the way ISBNs are written - 978-88-7524-166-7 - is exactly that, so it went through untouched and biblioteca cerca --isbn kept receiving the portal refusal this whole change exists to remove. Measured 2026-09-06: the portal answers (QR999) Operando con crt non validi, a refusal that carries a QRxxx code just like the threshold one, so the malformed-query detection had to stop keying on the absence of a code. The forms are now named one by one (a plain number, the ISIS range 260101/261231, an ISO date or range) and everything else is sanitised. Sanitising an ISBN is not enough on its own, and the right rewrite is not deducible from the value: two numeric fields of the same archive behave oppositely - on --dewey "340.5" the dot separates two real tokens and the spaced form finds the record, while an ISBN's punctuation formats a single number. The archive is also inconsistent with itself: record 9788875241667 is stored as one token and comes back only from the joined form, while another is stored as "978 88 98231-25-6" and comes back only from the spaced form. Neither spelling alone covers the catalogue, so an identifier field sends both in OR.
validated_outcome: biblioteca cerca --isbn "978-88-7524-166-7" goes from a portal refusal to the right record, leaving as ((9788875241667 O (978 88 7524 166 7)).ISBN); --isbn "978-88-98231-25-6", stored with separators, returns its own record from the same expression, and each spelling alone returns zero on the other one. --dewey "340.5" keeps the spaced rewrite that finds its record. A date range reaching BuildQuery unnormalised stays verbatim and is still refused loudly rather than answered wrongly.
